entities.name: TCR activation
observations: Primary human and mouse T cells retained activation-marker upregulation and proliferation when TCR-triggered extracellular superoxide was scavenged or NOX2 was absent. PMID:25081034.

entities.name: Extracellular superoxide
observations: TCR stimulation induces extracellular superoxide release, but scavenging abolished the signal without impairing primary T-cell activation, proliferation, or cytokine secretion. PMID:25081034.

entities.name: NOX2
observations: NOX2/gp91phox deficiency eliminated inducible extracellular superoxide yet preserved activation and proliferation; loss altered STAT5, Th1/Th2 differentiation, AKT signaling, Treg differentiation, and activation-induced death. PMID:25081034; PMID:22930452; PMID:27253713.

entities.name: PMID:25081034
observations: Anti-CD3/CD28 stimulation induced extracellular superoxide in primary T cells; SOD/ascorbate scavenging and NOX2 deficiency did not prevent activation-marker upregulation, proliferation, or cytokine secretion.

entities.name: PMID:22930452
observations: NOX2 deficiency changed CD4 T-cell differentiation and redox-sensitive STAT5 signaling but did not establish an obligatory activation requirement for extracellular superoxide.

entities.name: PMID:27253713
observations: Nox2-null T cells exhibited hyperactivation-associated phenotypes, including increased AKT phosphorylation and mitochondrial ROS, rather than activation failure.

entities.name: PMID:34583974
observations: Reduced mitochondrial ROS in SATB1-deficient CD4 T cells impaired TCR responses, and TFAM restoration rescued responses, supporting context-dependent intracellular mitochondrial redox signaling rather than extracellular-superoxide necessity.

entities.name: PMID:34784249
observations: DUOX1/2, but not NOX1/2, supported aspects of T-cell calcium signaling through a proposed redox metabolite cycle, showing that oxidase-dependent signaling is not equivalent to extracellular NOX2 superoxide.

entities.name: PMID:35481698
observations: Extracellular H2O2 scavenging altered intracellular ROS and CD8 memory differentiation but did not demonstrate a requirement for extracellular ROS in initial activation.
